In [[algebraic geometry]], an '''unramified morphism''' is a [[morphism of schemes|morphism]] <math>f: X \to Y</math> of [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]] such that (a) it is locally of finite presentation and (b) for each <math>x \in X</math> and <math>y = f(x)</math>, we have that
# The [[residue field]] <math>k(x)</math> is a [[separable algebraic extension]] of <math>k(y)</math>.
# <math>f^{\#}(\mathfrak{m}_y) \mathcal{O}_{x, X} = \mathfrak{m}_x, </math> where <math>f^{\#}: \mathcal{O}_{y, Y} \to \mathcal{O}_{x, X}</math> and <math>\mathfrak{m}_y, \mathfrak{m}_x</math> are [[maximal ideal]]s of the [[local ring]]s.

A flat unramified morphism is called an [[étale morphism]]. Less strongly, if <math>f</math> satisfies the conditions when restricted to sufficiently small neighborhoods of <math>x</math> and <math>y</math>, then <math>f</math> is said to be unramified near <math>x</math>.

Some authors prefer to use weaker conditions, in which case they call a morphism satisfying the above a '''G-unramified morphism'''.

== Simple example ==
Let <math>A</math> be a ring and ''B'' the ring obtained by adjoining an [[integral element]] to ''A''; i.e., <math>B = A[t]/(F)</math> for some [[monic polynomial]] ''F''. Then <math>\operatorname{Spec}(B) \to \operatorname{Spec}(A)</math> is unramified if and only if the polynomial ''F'' is [[Separable polynomial|separable]] (i.e., it and its derivative generate the unit ideal of <math>A[t]</math>).

== Curve case ==
Let <math>f: X \to Y</math> be a [[finite morphism]] between [[smooth variety|smooth]] connected [[curve]]s over an [[algebraically closed field]], ''P'' a [[closed point]] of ''X'' and <math>Q = f(P)</math>. We then have the local ring homomorphism <math>f^{\#} : \mathcal{O}_Q \to \mathcal{O}_P</math> where <math>(\mathcal{O}_Q, \mathfrak{m}_Q)</math> and <math>(\mathcal{O}_P, \mathfrak{m}_P)</math> are the local rings at ''Q'' and ''P'' of ''Y'' and ''X''. Since <math>\mathcal{O}_P</math> is a [[discrete valuation ring]], there is a unique integer <math>e_P > 0</math> such that <math>f^{\#} (\mathfrak{m}_Q) \mathcal{O}_P = {\mathfrak{m}_P}^{e_P}</math>. The integer <math>e_P</math> is called the '''ramification index''' of <math>P</math> over <math>Q</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Hartshorne|1977|loc=Ch. IV, § 2.}}</ref> Since <math>k(P) = k(Q)</math> as the base field is algebraically closed, <math>f</math> is unramified at <math>P</math> (in fact, [[étale morphism|étale]]) if and only if <math>e_P = 1</math>. Otherwise, <math>f</math> is said to be ramified at ''P'' and ''Q'' is called a [[branch point]].

== Characterization ==
Given a morphism <math>f: X \to Y</math> that is locally of finite presentation, the following are equivalent:<ref>{{harvnb|Grothendieck|Dieudonné|1967|loc=Corollary 17.4.2.}}</ref>
# ''f'' is unramified.
# The [[diagonal embedding|diagonal map]] <math>\delta_f: X \to X \times_Y X</math> is an open immersion.
# The relative [[cotangent sheaf]] <math>\Omega_{X/Y}</math> is zero.
